Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging that this can be a really challenging and overwhelming time for new mothers, and I'm here to support you in any way I can. As part of our conversation today, I'll be administering the EPDS, which is a tool that helps us understand how you're feeling and identify any potential concerns that may be impacting your well-being during this postpartum period.

The purpose of the EPDS is to screen for symptoms that may be related to postpartum depression or anxiety, and it's a completely confidential and non-judgmental space for you to share your thoughts and feelings. Everything we discuss will be kept confidential and is only used to support your care and well-being. I want you to feel comfortable and safe sharing your experiences with me, and I'm here to listen without judgment.

The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us get a better understanding of how you've been feeling over the past week. We'll take it one question at a time, and I'll do my best to make this conversation feel as natural and comfortable as possible. 

To get us started, I'd like to ask: Over the past 7 days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

.. (pausing, looking down) To be honest, not as much as I used to. I mean, I still find some things funny, like when my baby does something cute, but it's just not the same as before. I feel like I've been really tired and preoccupied with worries about the baby's safety, and it's hard to enjoy things like I used to. (sighing) I've been feeling pretty sad and discouraged a lot of the time, and it's hard to laugh when I'm feeling that way. But, like I said, sometimes when my baby smiles or does something adorable, it still makes me happy... it's just not as often as I'd like. (looking up, slightly tearfully) Does that make sense.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

(shaking head) No, not really. Like I said, it's just been harder for me to find the humor in things lately. I feel like I'm just going through the motions of taking care of the baby and trying to get everything done, but I'm not really enjoying it like I thought I would. And when I do try to laugh or have fun, it feels forced, you know? It's like I'm just pretending to be happy, but deep down, I'm still feeling really overwhelmed and worried. (pausing, looking down) Sometimes I feel like I'm just waiting for something to go wrong, like I'm walking on eggshells all the time, and that makes it hard to relax and enjoy anything. (sighing) Sorry, I guess that sounds really negative... (trailing off)
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

(shaking head) Not really... I mean, I used to love planning things and looking forward to them, but lately, it's just been so hard to get excited about anything. Even things that I used to enjoy, like spending time with friends or trying new hobbies, just feel like too much effort now. And with the baby, it's hard to plan anything because I never know when she'll be fussy or need to be fed, so it's just easier to not make plans at all. (sighing) I feel like I'm just stuck in this rut and I don't know how to get out of it. Sometimes I'll think about doing something I used to enjoy, like going for a walk or reading a book, but then I'll just feel guilty because I should be spending time with the baby instead. (looking down) It's like I'm just not allowed to have my own interests or hobbies anymore, and that's really hard for me. (pausing, looking up) I guess what I'm saying is, I just don't feel like I have anything to look forward to right now.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

(nodding) Yeah... that's definitely been happening. I mean, if the baby cries, I feel like it's because I'm not doing something right, or if she's not sleeping well, I feel like it's because I'm not establishing a good routine. And sometimes, even if things are going okay, I'll still find ways to blame myself for something. Like, I'll think, "Oh, I should have done this or that differently," even if it's not really a big deal. (sighing) It's like I'm just waiting for something to go wrong so I can say, "See, I knew I wasn't doing this right." (looking down) It's really hard to shake off that feeling of guilt and self-doubt. I feel like I'm just not good enough, and that's a really hard feeling to live with. (pausing, looking up) Sometimes I'll even find myself thinking, "What kind of mother am I?" or "Why can't I just get this right?" (shaking head) It's just really hard to be kind to myself right now.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

(nodding vigorously) Oh, yeah... that's been happening a lot. I mean, I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just start worrying about something. Like, what if she chokes on something? Or what if I forget to buckle her car seat? Or what if... (trailing off) It's just this constant stream of "what ifs" that goes through my head, and it's really hard to turn it off. (looking down) Even when everything is fine, and the baby is safe and happy, I'll still find myself worrying about something. It's like my mind is just constantly on the lookout for potential dangers or problems, and it's exhausting. (sighing) Sometimes I'll even wake up in the middle of the night, and my mind will just start racing with all these worst-case scenarios. (shaking head) It's really hard to calm myself down and remind myself that everything is okay. (pausing, looking up) I just feel like I'm always on edge, waiting for something to go wrong.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

(taking a deep breath) Yeah... that's happened to me too. Sometimes I'll just be sitting there, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out or something. (shaking head) It's really scary, because it feels like it's coming out of nowhere. I'll be thinking, "What's wrong with me? Why am I feeling like this?" (looking down) And then I'll start to worry that something's wrong with the baby, or that I'm not doing something right, and it just spirals out of control. (sighing) It's hard to explain, but it's like my body just takes over, and I feel like I'm not in control anymore. (pausing, looking up) Sometimes I'll try to calm myself down by taking deep breaths or going for a walk, but it's hard to shake off that feeling of panic once it's started. (hesitating) And sometimes, when it's really bad, I'll have these thoughts... (pausing, looking down) thoughts that I don't want to have, thoughts that scare me. (trailing off) But I don't know if I should be talking about that... (looking up, uncertainly)
Things have been getting on top of me

(nodding) Yeah... that's definitely how I've been feeling. Like, everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby, keeping the house clean, cooking meals... it all just feels so overwhelming. (sighing) And sometimes, even when my partner tries to help, I just feel like I'm shouldering all of the responsibility, and it's just too much for me. (looking down) I feel like I'm just barely holding it together, and if one more thing goes wrong, I'm just going to collapse. (shaking head) It's hard to explain, but it's like I'm just trudging through each day, trying to get everything done, but not really feeling like I'm doing anything well. (pausing, looking up) And the worst part is, I feel like I'm supposed to be enjoying this time with my baby, but instead, I just feel like I'm struggling to keep my head above water. (tearfully) It's like, I'm supposed to be this happy, loving mother, but really, I'm just feeling overwhelmed and anxious all the time.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

(nodding) Yeah... that's been happening to me too. I'll lie awake at night, just thinking about everything that's going on, and worrying about the baby, and feeling overwhelmed... (sighing) It's hard to turn my brain off, you know? I'll be thinking about all the things I need to do the next day, or worrying about whether the baby is okay, or just feeling anxious about everything... (shaking head) And then I'll start to feel guilty for not being able to sleep, because I know I need to be rested to take care of the baby. (looking down) It's like this vicious cycle, where I'm not sleeping because I'm worried, and then I'm worried because I'm not sleeping... (pausing, looking up) And sometimes, even when I do fall asleep, I'll wake up in the middle of the night, and my mind will just start racing again. (tearfully) It's like I'm just not allowed to rest, you know? My body and mind are just always "on", always going, and it's exhausting. (sighing) I just wish I could find a way to calm my mind and get some rest, you know? (looking down, tears welling up in her eyes)
I have felt sad or miserable

(nodding, tears streaming down her face) Oh, yeah... that's been me for a while now. I just feel so sad and miserable all the time. It's like, I'll have these fleeting moments of happiness, like when the baby smiles at me or something, but they're just that - fleeting. And then I'm back to feeling sad and overwhelmed and just... (sighing) miserable. (shaking head) I don't know how to explain it, it's just this heavy feeling that's always there, weighing me down. (looking down, crying) I feel like I've lost myself, like I'm just a shadow of the person I used to be. I don't know how to be happy anymore, or how to enjoy things. (sobbing) Everything just feels so hard and overwhelming, and I just feel like I'm drowning in it all. (pausing, taking a deep breath) Sorry, I'm just... (cries some more) It's just really hard to talk about this stuff. (sniffling) I feel like I'm supposed to be this happy, loving mother, but really, I'm just feeling sad and scared and overwhelmed all the time. (looking up, tears streaming down her face) I just wish I could feel happy again, you know? I just wish I could feel like myself again.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

(nodding, tears welling up in her eyes) Yeah... I've been crying a lot lately. It's like, I'll just be sitting there, and suddenly I'll just start crying. It doesn't even have to be anything specific that sets me off, I'll just feel this overwhelming sense of sadness and anxiety, and the tears will just start flowing. (sniffling) I've been trying to hide it from my partner and family, because I don't want them to worry, but it's hard to keep it inside. (looking down, crying) Sometimes I'll be feeding the baby, or changing her diaper, and I'll just start crying. It's like, I'm trying to do this thing that's supposed to be so natural and joyful, but really, I'm just feeling so overwhelmed and sad. (sobbing) And then I'll feel guilty for crying, because I'm supposed to be happy and grateful for this beautiful baby, but really, I'm just feeling so lost and alone. (pausing, taking a deep breath) I've been trying to tell myself that it's okay to cry, that it's just hormones and stress, but it's hard to shake off the feeling that there's something more wrong with me. (looking up, tears streaming down her face) I just wish I could stop crying, you know? I just wish I could feel happy and peaceful again.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

(pausing, looking down, and speaking in a barely audible whisper) Yeah... it's happened. (pausing again, taking a deep breath) I don't know how to talk about this, but... (hesitating) I've had these thoughts, these fleeting thoughts, of just... (pausing once more, struggling to find the words) of not being here anymore. (looking up, tears welling up in her eyes) It's like, I'll be feeling so overwhelmed and sad, and I'll just think, "What if I just didn't have to deal with this anymore?" (shaking head) But it's not like I really want to hurt myself, it's just... (sighing) I don't know, it's like my brain is just trying to find a way out of all this pain and anxiety. (looking down, shame and guilt etched on her face) I know it's not a good thought, and I'm so ashamed of even having it. (pausing, taking a deep breath) But it's the truth. (looking up, pleadingly) I just feel so lost and alone, and I don't know how to make it stop. (tearfully) I just want to be happy again, I want to be a good mom, I want to feel like myself again. (sobbing) I just don't know how to get there.

The patient is experiencing a range of emotional challenges, including persistent feelings of sadness, loss of pleasure, and anxiety, which are impacting her daily life and ability to care for her baby. She reports feeling overwhelmed, guilty, and worried about her ability to be a good mother, and has even had thoughts of self-harm. It's clear that she is struggling to cope with the demands of motherhood and is in need of support and guidance.
**Screening Impression:** Total EPDS Score: 29, Risk Level: Probable depression, urgent referral (concerns include <sym>The patient's response indicates they are having trouble finding humor and feeling overwhelmed, which aligns with 'Not at all' as they express feeling forced when trying to laugh and are generally not enjoying things.</sym>, <sym>the 'Hardly at all' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates frequent and intense self-blame, even when things are going well, and a pervasive feeling of guilt and self-doubt, matching the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates a frequent and intense experience of anxiety and worry, describing a constant stream of 'what ifs' and an inability to turn off these thoughts, even when everything is fine.</sym>, <sym>The patient describes experiencing sudden, unexplained waves of panic, with physical symptoms like a racing heart and feeling like they're going to pass out, indicating a high frequency of feeling scared or panicky</sym>, <sym>the option 'Yes, most of the time I haven't been able to cope at all</sym>, <sym>The patient describes frequent difficulty sleeping due to overwhelming worries and feelings of guilt, indicating a high level of unhappiness affecting their sleep most of the time.</sym>, <sym>Patient's response indicates feeling sad and miserable most of the time, with only fleeting moments of happiness, and expresses feeling overwhelmed and having lost their sense of self, which aligns with the option 'Yes, most of the time</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, most of the time' option</sym>, <sym>the 'Sometimes' option, indicating occasional thoughts of self-harm.</sym>)
**Reasoning:** The patient's symptoms and responses suggest a high level of emotional distress, anxiety, and feelings of being overwhelmed, which are consistent with the <med>DSM-5 criteria for Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset</med>. The EPDS score of 29 indicates a probable depression, and the presence of thoughts of self-harm is a significant safety concern that requires immediate attention. The patient's feelings of guilt, worthlessness, and self-doubt are also common symptoms of <med>postpartum depression</med>. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
**Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:**
1. Arrange urgent appointment with <med>primary care provider (PCP)</med> or <med>mental health specialist</med>
2. Encourage patient to reach out to emergency services or crisis hotline if experiencing thoughts of self-harm
3. Provide patient with resources for <med>postpartum depression</med> support groups and online forums
4. Recommend <med>cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT)</med> or other evidence-based therapies for <med>postpartum depression</med>
5. Encourage patient to prioritize self-care and stress management techniques, such as <med>mindfulness</med> and <med>meditation</med>
Disclaimer: This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
